tweets.text:
Open-weight models did not start the drop in price per unit of intelligence. They are a tailwind on a trend that was already underway.

For the last few years, a few factors have driven price drops:

1/ Model builders distilling their best models into smaller ones, with cheaper inference

2/ Infra efficiency

3/ Competition between model providers

You can see this pattern with every model company: Version x of the mid-size model = intelligence of version x-1 of the large model.  Same intelligence for less $.

Some communities are excited by AI’s impact on their field. Others are petrified. What’s the deciding factor(s)?

Some interesting machine & agent Vercel traffic stats.

• Across the entire Vercel network, 58.18% traffic is bot-originated (last 30d). This was 32% in Jan 2024.

• 60%+ of deployments on Vercel are now agentic, up from ~3% in Jan 2026.

• Up to 83% of pageviews are now coming from agents to Vercel's own documentation sites. The % reliably increases the more we optimize content for them.

I expect 'direct' human internet traffic to basically become a rounding error in coming years. The web will thrive, but it will be built for and by agents.

It's incredible to watch a new kind of economy be born. Agents purchasing infrastructure products and services. We've been shocked by how often they buy from our marketplace via our CLI already. We're now extending this to domains.

Agents can now go full stack, from idea to online business, with a banger domain name 😁

x.name: Aaron Levie
x.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI

tweets.text:
Agents spawning other agents, agents operating in the background on every task, and agent swarms will consume 1,000X more tokens than people prompting agents 1 at a time. 

The usage of AI as a chat system that can only work for you at the pace that you can prompt it will seem like a relic within a year or two. The vast, vast majority of tokens will be consumed by agents that are just doing continuous work for us in the background and in our workflows.

This is why we’re still so early in the curve of AI agent adoption right now, and how much more compute and infrastructure build out will be needed to sustain this.
